features.purpose: Key-value database with tables, bounded reads, chosen IDs, conditional patches, atomic increments, and transactions.

rules: Async SDK methods return Promises; db.tx.* factories return lazy thenables.

db.tx.* returns lazy operation handles. await/then/catch/finally and Promise.resolve/all consume them; repeated consumers share execution. db.transact requires distinct unconsumed handles from the current invocation; never await transaction children first. Build fresh handles per retry.

db.transact commits all members or none. Duplicate physical targets reject. Maximum 100 application actions/4 MiB; no chunking. Missing table catalogs are created separately before application writes. Chosen-ID collisions return null standalone and abort db.transact.

db.tx.update defaults to replacement/upsert. patch:true requires an existing record: omitted fields stay, undefined removes, null stores null, nested objects replace. if uses literal top-level field equality ANDed at commit (dots are part of a field name, not nested paths); undefined expects absence. Empty patches reject. Missing targets/failed conditions return false standalone and abort db.transact.
Import increment from @appdeploy/sdk; use only in top-level db.tx.update patch fields. Use it for shared counters instead of read-modify-write.

Narrow errors with isAppDatabaseError; use code, not message regexes. For known-aborted transactions, retry AppDatabaseConflict or applicable AppDatabaseConditionFailed with refreshed state, fresh handles, and a bounded budget. Reconcile AppDatabaseDuplicateId/AppDatabaseUnknownOutcome using the original receipt; never blindly retry unknown outcomes. AppDatabaseGatewayUnavailable alone does not authorize a write retry. Other write errors require explicit handling.

db.get defaults to eventual consistency. For reconciliation use { consistent: true }; reads are not a transaction-wide snapshot. AppDatabaseReadIncomplete is unresolved, not absence. Handle incomplete reads or read AppDatabaseGatewayUnavailable with a bounded read retry budget; quota/auth/limit failures must surface. Even consistent absence cannot rule out a pending commit.

Retain a stable application request ID across client errors and create its receipt in the same transaction as the effect. Verify owner/payload on replay; retain receipts after cancellation and never reuse IDs. Gate cancellation on active status. Seed with chosen-ID adds, never reset existing state.

Advanced writes include preparation/recovery costs. Standalone failures may follow committed items: details.settled lists known outcomes (null/false had no effect); unlisted outcomes remain unresolved.
For db.tx.*, logical table names must match [A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_.-]{0,127} and must not contain __ anywhere. Colons and arbitrary user IDs are invalid; use an encoded/hash-derived safe key.
If a deployed SDK lacks methods documented here, regenerate its bundle. Inspect the SDK's databaseContract for its revision and available capabilities. Never invent missing methods.
db.set does not exist. Legacy db.add generates physical IDs independently of payload id; db.tx.add uses record.id when provided and never overwrites it.
db.add returns string|null array with ID (success) or null (failure) per record.
db.update/delete return boolean arrays indicating success per item.
db.list returns items with each database ID attached as id:string, plus an optional nextToken for pagination.
db.get returns stored record data in the same order as the requested IDs, with null for missing IDs. It does not attach the database ID to returned records; retain and reuse the ID passed to db.get.
Legacy db.update replaces the full record (no merge). Prefer db.tx.update with patch:true for field edits; get/spread/update can lose concurrent edits. Use increment for shared counters.
db.get uses database IDs (usually returned by db.add). If the server mints an ID, return it to the client and reuse it - don't generate a second ID.
db.list filters run after reads and do not reduce cost; limit counts evaluated, not matching, items. Never use filtered lists for lookups on growing tables.

DB reads and writes have per-app minute and daily quotas; never hide or retry 429 AppDatabaseQuotaExceeded. Each complete serialized item, including nested data and keys, must be at most 256 KiB; count caps are not size checks, so split by bytes or store large arrays and blobs in storage.

Every db.* call has a 1 MiB serialized-input limit, and db.add, db.get, db.update, and db.delete accept at most 500 array elements per call. Split larger work by both serialized byte size and item count.

Prefer db.get with saved IDs or a bounded logical table such as `notes_<safeUserKey>`. Encode/hash arbitrary user IDs into a table-safe key. Keep pages small, follow nextToken only when needed, and never drain all pages in one request or cron.
Cron jobs must checkpoint and process only changes, never rescan growing tables.
